concepts.def: How the eye changes lens shape to focus near or far
Ring of muscle that changes lens shape
Skin blood vessels widen to release more heat
Skin blood vessels narrow to keep heat

walkthroughs.body_html:
The lens changes shape to focus light.

Near object: ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments loosen, lens becomes fat and round.

Far object: ciliary muscles relax, ligaments pull tight, lens becomes thin and flat.

Myopia (short sight): image forms in front of the retina. Fixed with a concave (diverging) lens.

Hyperopia (long sight): image forms behind the retina. Fixed with a convex (converging) lens.

Other options: contact lenses, laser eye surgery, or replacement lenses.

The thermoregulatory centre in the brain monitors blood temperature.

Too hot: sweating (evaporation cools you), vasodilation, hairs lie flat.

Too cold: shivering (muscles release heat), vasoconstriction, hairs stand up to trap a warm air layer.
